full_judgment:
Md Moinul Islam Chowdhury, J: At the instance of the present accused-appellant, Syed Toufique Ahmed, this appeal has been preferred against the legality of the impugned Order No. 05 dated 7-6-2017 passed by the learned Judge of Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka in the. Cyber Tribunal Case No. 195 of 2016 arising out of Guishan Police Station Case No. 18 dated 20-5-2016 under section 57 of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (as amended up to 2013), now pending before the Cyber Tribunal . (Bangladesh), Dhaka without considering the application under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 and thereby framing charge under section 57 of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (as amended up to 2013) against the accused-appellant. 

 2. The relevant facts for disposal of this appeal, inter alia, are that the present respondent No. 2 Md Abdul Hannan Ratan as the informant lodged the FIR/ejahar being Gulshan Police Station Case No. 18 dated 20-5-2016 under section 57 of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (as amended in 2013) alleging that the informant is a Member of the Committee Secretary and Central Sub-committee Joint Secretary of Brahmanbaria District Awami League and he is a businessman and honorary member of FBCCI and Treasurer and Director of India Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industries. On the other hand, the accused-appellant is a member of Kadiani Community and also a banker by profession. The co-accused-respondent 3 is the wife of the informant and they married in the year of 1998 and during their wedlock one boy and two girls were born. The accused-appellant regularly maintained a friendly relationship with the informant and co-accused-respondent No. 3. The accused-appellant estab-lished an extra-marital relationship with his wife upon which the Gulshan Police Station Case No. 19 dated 30-3-2016 was filed against the present accused-appellant under sections 380, 497 and 498 of the Penal Code. 

 3. At the time of investigation of the above case, the informant came to know that there were house obscene message communications taken between the accused-appellant and the co-accused-respondent No. 3 (the wife of the informant) during the period of 3-3-2016 to 28-3-2016 by the mobile phone number 01715280280, 01732241652 and 01747256293. The informant came to know that the present accused publicly disclosed those messages with an intention to tarnish reputation and fame his wife intentionally exchanged above obscene text messages to the informant. The messages were passed within the Brahmanbaria District, as such, the reputation was lower down, thereby, the present accused-appellant and the co-accused-respondent No. 3 have committed offences under section 57(2) of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (as amended in 2013). 

 4. At the initiation of the case, the Gulshan Police Station wanted to make quire to the accused-appellant on remand but those applications were rejected. However, after investigation the police submitted the charge sheet No. 115 dated 27-7-2016 under section 57(2) of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (as amended in 2013). The accused-appellant later on granted bail by the learned Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka. 

 8. Mr SM Shahjahan, the learned Advocate, appearing along with Mr Md Shibbir Ahmed. the learned Advocate for the accused-appellant submits that the Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka erred in law as well as facts and circumstances of the case with wrong finding and misconceived with facts and evidence on record thereby came to an erroneous decision and framed charge against the accused-appellant and hence the charge framing Order is liable to be set-aside. 

 10. He also submits that the accused-appellant should be tried in the earlier GR Case filed under the provisions of the Penal Code and the impugned Order has been passed mechanically and without giving reasons for framing charge which is not expected from the learned Cyber Tribunal, therefore, this appeal should be allowed. 

 11. Mr Md Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury, the learned Senior Advocate, appearing along with the learned Advocate Mr Mohammad Shafikul Islam Ripon appearing for the informant-respondent No. 2 Md Abdul Hannan Ratan submits that the informant filed the FIR alleging an extra-marital relationship between the accused-appellant and the co-accused-respondent No. 3 (his wife) a case was filed which is pending and during investigation of the said case. The police recovered a huge volume of text messages between the accused-appellant and co-accused-respondent No. 3 (his wife) which are obscene, false and which have tarnished his reputation and the local supporters of the informant became annoyed, as such, he has filed the 2nd Case against both the accused-appellant and his wife under section 57(2) of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (as amended in 2013). After hearing the parties the learned Judge of Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka considered the materials in front of him and framed charge against both the accused by rejecting the application filed under section 265C of the CrPC, as such, there is no illegality committed by the learned Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka and the appeal should be dismissed. 

 12. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial of the case has been initiated by the Tribunal by recording depositions of PW 1 the informant Md Abdul Hannan Ratan who was cross-examined but this appeal has been filed in order to cause delay in the GR Case pending in the learned Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka under section 57(2) of the Ain where admittedly obscene message, conversations and communications, therefore, the learned Tribunal lawfully framed charge against both the accused, as such, no interference is called for from this Court. 

 13. Considering the above submissions of the learned Advocates for both the sides and also considering the petition of appeal filed under section 84 of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (as amended in 2013) along with the impugned Order passed by the learned Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka by the Order No. 5 dated 7-6-2017, it appears to us that the present informant-respondent No. 2 was involved with the some political and some business organizations in the District of Brahmanbaria and he was married to the co-accused-respondent No. 3 and 3 children were born in their conjugal life. It further appears that the present accused-appellant was a family friend of the informant and his wife but there is an allegation of extra-marital relationship with the accused-appellant and the wife of the informant which caused the informant to file a GR Case against the accused-appellant under sections 380, 497 and 498 of the Penal Code and during the investigation of the said case the investigators revealed some obscene text message conversations between the accused-appellant and co-accused-respondent No. 3 (wife of the informant) during the period of 3-3-2016 to 28-3-2016 which prompted the informant to file another Police Station Case against the present accused-appellant under section 57(2) of the Act, 2006. After submitting a charge sheet upon the above allegations the police submitted a charge sheet disclosing some materials of communication of obscene and false text messages between the accused which were disclosed in the public within the District of Brahmanbaria where the informant had high reputation both politically and as a businessman. On the basis of the charge sheet the learned Cyber Tribunal framed charged by the impugned Order has been challenged preferring this appeal. 

 17. We have perused the relevant provision of the Act, 1913 in particular section 2(26) of the Act, 2006 (as amended in 2013) which contains that the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 would be the procedural law for continuing with the case filed under section 57(2) of the Act, 2006 (as amended in 2013). We have also gone through sections 57, 84 and other relevant provisions of the said Act. In the instant case, the allegations were made by the informant impleading both the accused for commission of offence under section 57(2) of the Act which were examined by the learned Cyber Tribunal before concluding to frame charge against both the accused for commission of offence and the impugned Order and the learned Cyber Tribunal framed charge under section 242 of the CrPC after forming an opinion that there is a ground for assuming that the accused might have committed an offence. A Court can frame charge. The Court would ask the accused whether he admits as to the commission of the offence for which he has been charged. 

 18. In the instant case, the Cyber Tribunal has properly formed his opinion and presumed as to the offence as alleged legally and lawfully framed in order to conclusion of the case. 

 22. The learned Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka is hereby directed to continue with the trial of the case and conclude the trial within 9 (nine) months from the receipt of this Judgment and Order without allowing any adjournment either of the parties. 

 23. The interim order of stay granted at the time of admission of the petition of appeal in the Cyber Tribunal Case No. 195 of 2016 is hereby recalled and vacated.
